title: [B2 • Band 6.0] Bài 204: The Vertical Agrarian Revolution in Singapore
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 204 (LEVEL B2 • BAND 6.0)

The Vertical Agrarian Revolution in Singapore

Paragraph 1. Singapore faces a striking geographic challenge. With nearly six million residents living on just 730 square kilometres, the city-state has long prioritized high-rise public housing, shipping ports, and commercial districts over farmland. Consequently, Singapore imports over ninety percent of its total food supply, exposing the nation to shipping disruptions and climate-related crop failures overseas. To reduce these risks, the Singapore Food Agency launched the '30 by 30' plan, seeking to grow thirty percent of the country's nutritional needs locally by 2030, using under one percent of total land without taking away residential or industrial zones.

Paragraph 2. To meet this target, local farming firms are replacing soil fields with indoor vertical hydroponics. Leading this shift is GroFarm, a technology-driven enterprise operating inside a converted multi-storey logistics warehouse in northern Singapore. Its facility runs an automated rotating tower standing nine metres high. Seedlings of bok choy, kale, and Chinese spinach sit in shallow plastic troughs bathed in circulating nutrient liquid made from recycled water, potassium, nitrogen, and essential minerals. By replacing soil with closed water loops, the design cuts water consumption by ninety-five percent compared with open-field farming.

Paragraph 3. The key operational advantage of indoor farming is complete climate insulation. Automated sensors regulate humidity, temperature, and carbon dioxide continuously, while high-efficiency LED panels emit tailored wavelengths of blue and deep red light optimized for photosynthesis, removing dependence on unpredictable sunshine. Because the building is tightly sealed against outdoor pests and soil bacteria, GroFarm grows crops completely free from synthetic pesticides and reaches up to twelve harvest cycles annually, compared with four harvests on regional outdoor farms.

Paragraph 4. Nevertheless, the vertical farming model faces strong economic doubts centered on energy consumption. Whereas rural farms enjoy free sunlight, indoor facilities burn vast amounts of power to run thousands of LED fixtures and air-conditioning units needed to remove heat generated by indoor lamps. In Singapore, where power generation relies largely on imported natural gas, high electricity bills can account for up to forty percent of an indoor farm's operating budget. As a result, locally grown hydroponic greens typically sell for fifteen to twenty percent more in supermarkets than field-grown produce imported from Malaysia or Thailand.

Paragraph 5. To narrow this price gap, agricultural scientists are pursuing biological and engineering improvements. Researchers at the Singapore Institute of Food Innovation are breeding compact, fast-maturing vegetable cultivars designed specifically for artificial lighting. Meanwhile, engineers are testing rooftop solar panels and heat-recovery pumps to lower dependence on the national power grid. Furthermore, government procurement subsidies require public hospitals, schools, and military bases to purchase a minimum quota of greens from domestic vertical suppliers, offering a practical testbed for urban food security.

groups.title: Questions 7–12
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 3: "...emit tailored wavelengths of blue and deep red light..."
Đoạn 4: "...high electricity bills can account for up to forty percent..."

q7.text: The '30 by 30' plan requires farms to take over large sections of residential neighbourhoods.

steps: Đoạn 1: Dùng dưới 1% diện tích đất và không lấy đất khu dân cư hay công nghiệp (without taking away residential or industrial zones).

q8.text: GroFarm operates inside a building previously built for storage and logistics.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...operating inside a converted multi-storey logistics warehouse..."

q9.text: Hydroponic crops grown indoors require smaller quantities of chemical plant nutrients than traditional field crops.

steps: Đoạn 2 & 3: Bài có nói tiết kiệm 95% nước và không dùng thuốc trừ sâu, nhưng không so sánh lượng chất dinh dưỡng hóa học với nông trại truyền thống.

q10.text: Locally grown hydroponic vegetables currently sell for less in supermarkets than vegetables imported from Thailand.

steps: Đoạn 4: Đắt hơn 15–20% (sell for fifteen to twenty percent more), không phải rẻ hơn.

q11.text: Engineers are testing rooftop solar power to lower the farms' reliance on the national electricity grid.

steps: Đoạn 5: "...testing rooftop solar panels... to lower dependence on the national power grid."

q12.text: Government procurement subsidies help guarantee institutional buyers from public facilities for local vertical farms.

steps: Đoạn 5: Trợ giá thu mua bắt buộc bệnh viện công, trường học và doanh trại quân đội phải mua hạn ngạch tối thiểu từ các trang trại đứng.
